heroHeadline: Kast's Own Coalition Revolts Against His Security-Reform State of Exception as Approval Slides Toward 57% Disapproval
heroSubtitle: President José Antonio Kast's ACOT constitutional security reform, signed August 10 and creating a new 240-day presidential state of exception, drew escalating cross-partisan backlash through late August: Cadem polling shifted from 58% opposed to unilateral presidential power (Aug 20) to 49% opposed with disapproval of Kast at 57% (Aug 24). On August 25, Senate President Paulina Núñez — from Kast's own Renovación Nacional ally — publicly called to withdraw the state-of-exception clause, warning it lacked even the ruling coalition's votes; the government dropped the bill's legislative fast-track in response, and Kast pressed his coalition for 'political will' at a PDI vehicle-delivery ceremony the same day. The reform controversy unfolded against the backdrop of the Chamber's August 18 vote extending the Macrozona Sur state of exception 30 more days and copper's all-time record of US$6.736/lb on the LME (Aug 17).
footerNote: Data sourced from official Chilean government records (Biblioteca del Congreso, Banco Central, SERVEL), Rettig and Valech commissions, IACHR, CIPER Chile, and major international outlets.
